title: Argus
description: An Argus image, argus many eyes, fills the frame with looking: extra pupils on a body, a swarm of viewpoints, a creature or a city of eyes. The surplus is seeing, counted as organs or cameras, not as flare.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Surveillance becomes anatomy. A wall of cameras.
A god covered in irises. Use it when paranoia, divinity, or the internet should be visible as too much seeing.
It is the wrong tool for a single honest portrait, and for a tidy split of two scenes. If the same person repeats as clones, that is duplication.
If the frame is divided into panels, that is split screen. If facets mirror one image, that is a kaleidoscope.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Count the eyes. Place them as objects: on skin, on walls, as a field of viewpoints around a still center.
Keep a readable subject so the swarm has a king. Light each iris with a small catchlight if they are organs.
If they are cameras, give each lens a tiny practical. Do not dissolve them into noise.
Prompt an Argus image of the subject: many eyes, many viewpoints, a creature or a city of looking.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Duplication repeats a person. Argus multiplies looking, not necessarily the whole body.
Split Screen divides the frame into panels of action. Argus can be one composition swarming with eyes.
Kaleidoscope mirrors facets. Here the eyes are the point.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is flare on a face, or a Split Screen. The tell is no extra eyes as objects, or a tidy two-way divide.
The fix is countable pupils or viewpoints, a swarm with a center.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Argus in film?
Argus is many eyes and many viewpoints: a creature or a city of looking. One gaze is not enough. Looking becomes a swarm.
Argus vs duplication
Duplication repeats a person in the frame. Argus multiplies eyes or viewpoints. You may still have one body. The surplus is seeing.
When should I use Argus?
Use it for paranoia, gods, networks of watching. Skip it on a single honest portrait, and skip it when you only need two panels of action.
How do I prompt Argus for AI image or video?
Write Argus image of [Subject], many eyes, many viewpoints. Count them. Keep a center so it is not noise. Eyes should be objects, not flare.
